mission: Torin's technique works — the void around him reaches the Scar. The wound begins to close. His plan is functioning. And the cost is visible: Torin is diminishing. The technique is replacing him.
why_now: The climax's second crisis — Torin succeeding at the cost of himself
conflict: Torin's plan works: the technique applied at the Scar is closing the wound. But Maetha's warning is proving true in real time — prolonged use is erasing Torin's emotional range, his personality, his humanity. The caldera doesn't consume. It replaces.
turning_point: Torin's voice, from inside the void: still articulate but emotionally hollow. He's speaking with the precision of someone who remembers how to form sentences but has forgotten why they matter. He's becoming infrastructure — exactly what Gavran's seal was.
opening_hook: The wound is closing. Torin is winning. And Sera is screaming his name.
closing_hook: Sera moves toward the void. Ben reaches for her — 'Sera, don't—' She looks back. 'I was sealed once. I will not watch it happen to someone else and do nothing.' She enters the void.
emotional_trajectory: Horror at Torin's diminishment -> Sera's desperate determination -> the choice to save him

stakes.personal: Torin being consumed by the technique — Maetha's prophecy fulfilling
stakes.interpersonal: Sera choosing to save Torin despite everything — love without control
stakes.external: The wound closing but at the cost of another living person becoming infrastructure

setting: Veranthos — the Scar, Torin's void expanding, the wound closing
sensory_details: Torin's void — the lattice absent around him, a zone of formless Force; his voice: still speaking but the warmth gone, the humor gone, just words without person; Sera's face — grief and iron; the wound visibly closing — the Scar narrowing
notes: Maetha's warning payoff — the most important promise in the book. Torin's diminishment should be specific and terrible: not dramatic dark-side corruption but the slow subtraction of personality. He's becoming what Gavran became — infrastructure.
